note: Independent rejudgment 2026-10-11 (judge did not author a832af8548 or the tests); replaces the author's pending-confirmation note. RFC 8907 Section 4.3: "The client MUST accommodate such closures on a TCP session even after Single Connection Mode has been established." The closures meant are the server's, e.g. the inactivity timeout of the preceding sentence. Positive TestRFC8907ServerClosureOfPooledConnectionIsAccommodated: newSessionServer echo=true answers the first request with TAC_PLUS_SINGLE_CONNECT_FLAG, so Single Connection Mode is established in the first two packets; closeAfter=1 then closes the idle TCP and waitClosed confirms it before session 2, which must PASS on a second connection carrying exactly one request. Negative TestRFC8907ClosureMidSessionOnPooledConnectionIsAccommodated: midExchangeCloser echoes the flag, counts [2] prove two sessions shared the established TCP, then the server reads session 3's request and closes unanswered; session 3 must still PASS and counts must be [3,1]. Producer: client.go sendReceive retries once on pooledConnErr with a fresh dial after trySend's closeAndEvict; trySend returns pooledConnErr only for a reused (established) connection, so the fresh-dial closure correctly surfaces as an error. Removing that retry fails both: session 2/3 would read EOF on the evicted TCP and authenticatePass would see an error. Both units sit on an established single-connect TCP, isolate the closure, and assert the exact outcome (PASS plus the connection and request counts). Limit kept on record: the two discrimination records are revert halts of sendReceive, not a break of the retry alone, so question 2 is answered here by reading, not by a recorded break. Verdict enforced confirmed.
